process_area.title: Job Site Delivery Execution & Material Handling

fields.Participants: Driver, Delivery Crew, Contractor Site Foreman

workflows.name: Job Site Delivery Unloading & Material Placement

Automation Opportunity: - Delivery scheduling auto-optimized from the route/dock/traffic data; real-time tracking auto-pushed to customer and store; POD auto-captured digitally
Controls: - CTL-452 (ensure controlled execution — Job Site Delivery Execution & Material Handling (PA-74.2).)
- operational: Driver / Delivery Crew sign-off on the workflow output
Pain Points / Risks: - **Delivery-failure risk**: a delivery misses its window (traffic, access, scheduling), disrupting the customer/project; mitigated by the real-time tracking and the rescheduling protocol

- **Data-quality risk**: incomplete or inaccurate master data (pricing, inventory, customer) corrupts the workflow output; mitigated by the master-data governance (VS-29 / W291) and the periodic audit
System Touchpoints: - Order management (links to VS-08 / W536 unified order management, VS-60 / W2286 routing)
- Logistics/DC (links to VS-04 / W3 receiving, VS-04 / W52 fleet, VS-77 / material staging)
Time Estimate: - Absorbed into the Driver / Delivery Crew role; not incremental headcount unless volume scales significantly.

steps.activity: Driver arrives at site: contacts foreman, confirms unloading location, verifies site access and safety (hard hat area, PPE required); positions truck
Delivery crew and contractor personnel unload: hand-bomb materials if no forklift/crane; place in designated staging area per contractor direction; separate by type and phase
Site foreman verifies delivery against manifest: counts items, notes damage or shortage, signs receipt; Driver photographs delivered materials as proof

steps.activity: Contractor reports damage or shortage with photos; Trade Sales Rep logs incident in ERP; severity classification: minor (<PHP 5K), moderate, major (>PHP 50K)
Logistics Coordinator investigates: reviews driver photos, checks loading records; determines responsibility (BuildRight, 3PL, contractor)
Resolution: replacement within 48 hours for BuildRight-caused issues; credit note for shortages; LP investigates patterns; 3PL liability claim for carrier damage

steps.activity: Driver collects POD: signed receipt from foreman (paper or electronic), photographs of materials at placement, GPS coordinates, delivery timestamp
System uploads POD data: matches to delivery order, records GPS and timestamp, stores photos; auto-matches to sales order for billing
Finance uses POD for billing: triggers invoice for trade accounts; settles 3PL payment upon confirmed delivery; archives for 10 years per BIR

fields.Participants: Driver, Safety Officer, Contractor Site Safety Manager
fields.Trigger: Truck arrives at active construction site

workflows.name: Contractor Site Safety Compliance During Delivery

Automation Opportunity: - Delivery scheduling auto-optimized from the route/dock/traffic data; real-time tracking auto-pushed to customer and store; POD auto-captured digitally
Controls: - CTL-452 (ensure controlled execution — Job Site Delivery Execution & Material Handling (PA-74.2).)
- CTL-452 (compliance-monitoring — links to VS-22); Operational: Driver sign-off on the workflow output
Pain Points / Risks: - **Delivery-failure risk**: a delivery misses its window (traffic, access, scheduling), disrupting the customer/project; mitigated by the real-time tracking and the rescheduling protocol
- **Non-compliance risk**: a regulatory requirement is missed (DTI permit, data privacy, AML), creating a fine or complaint; mitigated by the compliance-checklist and the regulatory-monitoring
System Touchpoints: - Order management (links to VS-08 / W536 unified order management, VS-60 / W2286 routing)
- Compliance/risk (links to VS-22 / regulatory, VS-86 / AML, VS-91 / privacy)
- Logistics/DC (links to VS-04 / W3 receiving, VS-04 / W52 fleet, VS-77 / material staging)
Time Estimate: - Frequency: Per delivery to active sites
- Absorbed into the Driver role; not incremental headcount unless volume scales significantly.

steps.activity: Driver dons required PPE: hard hat, safety vest, safety shoes; attends site safety briefing; identifies hazards (excavations, overhead work, equipment)
Driver follows site-specific safety rules: speed limit, designated routes, prohibited areas, emergency assembly point; reports unsafe conditions
Safety Officer conducts random compliance checks; tracks safety incident rate (target: zero); incorporates into driver training

workflows.name: Bulk Material Handling at Job Site

Automation Opportunity: - Material-demand auto-forecast from the project schedule; delivery-phasing auto-sequenced; site-reconciliation auto-tracked from the delivery-vs-installed delta
Controls: - CTL-452 (ensure controlled execution — Job Site Delivery Execution & Material Handling (PA-74.2).)
- operational: Logistics Coordinator sign-off on the workflow output
Pain Points / Risks: - **Execution risk**: process variability or system failure disrupts the workflow's output; mitigated by the documented procedure and the system controls

- **Data-quality risk**: incomplete or inaccurate master data (pricing, inventory, customer) corrupts the workflow output; mitigated by the master-data governance (VS-29 / W291) and the periodic audit
System Touchpoints: - Logistics/DC (links to VS-04 / W3 receiving, VS-04 / W52 fleet, VS-77 / material staging)
Time Estimate: - Absorbed into the Logistics Coordinator role; not incremental headcount unless volume scales significantly.

steps.activity: Logistics Coordinator arranges bulk delivery (sand, gravel, cement): requires dump trucks; coordinates with DSD vendor or 3PL; confirms contractor has designated dump area
Driver delivers: positions dump truck, tips load carefully; contractor foreman visually estimates quantity; photographs tipped load
System processes bulk delivery: catch-weight recorded with estimated weight; Finance bills based on delivered weight; Logistics tracks cost per cubic meter

steps.activity: Contractor identifies quality concern at delivery: lumber grade mismatch, tile color variation, cement moisture damage, steel dimension off-spec; refuses affected items
Trade Sales Rep escalates: Quality Inspector visits site within 24 hours to assess; compares against specification and order agreement
Resolution: valid issue — replacement within 48 hours, vendor claim filed; specification misunderstanding — clarifies and offers exchange; Category Manager updates product description

- System auto-alert of "notifies contractor with updated ETA" (replaces manual Step 3).

steps.activity: System sends automated ETA notification to contractor when dispatched: estimated arrival, driver name and contact, vehicle plate, delivery contents summary
Driver updates status in mobile app: departed, en route (GPS tracking), arrived, unloading started, complete; contractor tracks via app
Logistics Coordinator manages ETA exceptions: if delayed >30 min, notifies contractor with updated ETA; tracks on-time delivery rate (target: ≥90%)
